subject: Service guarantee language and monthly credit structure — Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Alice Green <alice.green@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Nimbus standard SLA (template attached)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. Our procurement team has attached Nimbus Health's standard SLA template (Nimbus_SLA_Template_v2.docx). Two items we need you to confirm before we can move legal:

- Uptime target of 99.9% for hosted API (we can discuss higher targets for Dedicated).
- Monthly service credit up to 100% of the affected month for prolonged outages (procurement insists on full reimbursement as a last-resort).
- Latency objective: P95 <= 300ms for standard text-generation routes; P99 <= 800ms.

Can you review and let us know which items Redwood can accept as-is, and which require carveouts? If you have a redline, please send it back so our legal team can take a look.

Appreciate a quick reply — we're aiming to finalize by end of month.

Best,
Alice
Alice Green
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health
alice.green@nimbushealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Green <alice.green@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus standard SLA (template attached)

Hi Alice — thanks for sending this over and for the useful product feedback. Looping in Laura (legal) and Priyom (sales ops) to keep this thread consolidated.

Quick summary of Redwood's position and proposed edits (we attached a concise response PDF):

1) Uptime targets:
   - Hosted API (shared pool): our standard commercial uptime in template is 99.9% for the hosted tier; for larger commitments we offer 99.95% on dedicated reservations.

2) Monthly credits / cap:
   - We can agree to a monthly credit ladder (detailed below), but we do not typically accept uncapped 100% refunds for hosted production. For hosted customers we propose a capped remedy schedule; for Dedicated we can be more flexible.

3) Latency:
   - Recommended SLOs: P95 <= 500ms, P99 <= 1s for the primary text-generation route. The 300ms P95 target you requested is achievable on Dedicated capacity for provisioned traffic patterns; on shared-hosted workloads it depends on burst profile and model choice.

4) Maintenance and carveouts:
   - Scheduled maintenance (48h notice) and force majeure are carveouts; emergency mitigations and regional failover are handled via our incident playbooks.

Proposed monthly credit ladder (hosted):
   - Uptime >= 99.95%: 0% credit
   - 99.50% <= Uptime < 99.95%: 10% of monthly invoice
   - 99.00% <= Uptime < 99.50%: 25% of monthly invoice
   - Uptime < 99.00%: 100% of monthly invoice (full credit)

We are willing to increase the hosted cap to 75% of the month (for the first 12 months of the contract) as a commercial concession while we prove production performance. For Dedicated customers we can agree a higher cap on an account-by-account basis.

I'll attach Redwood_SLA_Response_20270722.pdf with inline suggestions. If that looks reasonable, Laura can produce a contract redline for your legal.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Alice Green <alice.green@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-23T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus standard SLA (template attached)

Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the ladder. Procurement's two pushes: (1) they are uncomfortable with any cap below 100% for hosted; (2) they want the latency commitments closer to our 300ms P95 ask.

We can consider the 75% transitional cap, but only if Redwood agrees to both:
- A formal remediation & prioritization plan whenever uptime falls into the 99.00-99.50% band (i.e., guaranteed patch/mitigation timelines and weekly updates until resolved).
- Access to incident logs and a post-incident report within 72 hours of incident closure.

On latency: if Redwood can promise the 300ms P95 on our primary model (we'll share prompt mix), we'd be open to keeping hosted. Otherwise Nimbus will lean toward Dedicated for production-sensitive routes.

Can you confirm those two asks? Also — please send the redline when available.

Thanks,
Alice

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Green <alice.green@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-24T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus standard SLA (template attached)

On Fri, Jul 23, 2027 at 09:14 AM Alice Green <alice.green@nimbushealth.com> wrote:
> Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the ladder. Procurement's two pushes: (1) they are uncomfortable with any cap below 100% for hosted; (2) they want the latency commitments closer to our 300ms P95 ask.

Hi Alice — appreciate the clarity. We can do the following compromise to keep things moving without exposing our hosted customers to open-ended financial risk:

1) Cap and remediation:
   - Hosted cap: increase to 75% of the monthly invoice for the first 12 months (as previously noted). After 12 months, revert to a 50% cap unless usage/metrics justify otherwise.
   - Remediation commitment: when uptime falls into 99.00-99.50% band, Redwood will provide 
       * Incident triage within 4 business hours,
       * A written mitigation plan within 48 hours, and
       * Weekly status updates until the issue is resolved.
   - We agree to provide incident logs and a post-incident report within 48 hours of incident closure (we'll redact sensitive platform operational details as needed).

2) Latency:
   - For your primary model mix, if you move to a dedicated reservation we will guarantee P95 <= 300ms as part of the capacity sizing. For hosted, we can commit to completing a performance validation run (using your prompt mix) during onboarding; if it fails to meet the target we will provide a migration offer to a dedicated pool with reduced provisioning lead time.

3) Language to include in the contract: a short clause that credits are "sole and exclusive remedy" for outages, plus an explicit quarterly SLA review with your technical team.

I've attached Redwood_SLA_Redline_for_Nimbus_20270724.docx with the exact suggested wording and the credit math formula. If that aligns with procurement, I'll ask Laura to circulate a legal redline this week.

Marcus

From: Alice Green <alice.green@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-26T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus standard SLA (template attached)

Marcus — appreciate the flexibility. Procurement is prepared to accept the 75% hosted cap for the first 12 months if Redwood agrees to the remediation timelines and the 48-hour post-incident report commitment. They also want the "sole and exclusive remedy" wording limited to monetary credits for service unavailability (they prefer this to exclude data security/regulatory breaches).

Two minor asks before we hand to legal:
- Make the remediation timeline language explicit in the redline (48 hours for mitigation plan; weekly updates thereafter).
- Add a quarterly SLA review clause with defined attendees (Nimbus: Alice, Platform Lead; Redwood: Marcus, Priyom, and the Account's SOC lead).

If you can include those two bullets in the redline now, we'll have our counsel send back a final redline and signature copy next week.

I'll wait for the updated doc.

Best,
Alice
